description: Incident and malfunction report for a slot game system, including regulator notification content. See steering/incident-malfunction-handling.md.
instructions: Sequence is: STOP the affected game or feature, PRESERVE evidence, SCOPE the impact, THEN fix. Fixing first risks deploying an uncertified build and destroying the evidence needed to scope player impact.
Answer the three impact questions separately. 'Did it affect game fairness', 'did it affect player funds' and 'did it affect a compliance function' have different notification consequences.
Do not minimise. Regulators tolerate proactive, complete and timely notification far better than the later discovery that something was concealed.

severityLevels.P1: Affects game fairness or outcome correctness. RNG anomaly, payout calculation error, RTP deviating from the declared value, uncertified build in production. Notify immediately.
severityLevels.P2: Affects player funds or a compliance function. Wallet balance error, double debit, self-exclusion failure, limits not enforced, excluded player able to play. Notify immediately.
severityLevels.P3: Affects service availability but not outcome correctness. Game will not load, abnormal disconnect rate, game recall unavailable. Notification depends on the market.
severityLevels.P4: Presentation layer only. Animation or text defect not involving rules or disclosure. Record only.

alwaysP1OrP2: Non-CSPRNG used for outcome determination, however limited the scope
Self-excluded player able to bet, including via central system fail-open
Actual RTP systematically deviating from the declared value
Audit log lost or found to be mutable
Stake limit not enforced (UK GBP 5 / GBP 2, German tiering)

incident.detectionMethod: monitoring-alert | player-report | internal-testing | operator-report | regulator-enquiry | audit

impactAssessment.scopingLimitations: State explicitly if the impact could not be fully scoped, and why

playerRemediation.principle: Where facts are unclear, the cost should be absorbed by the operator. Treatment favourable to the player carries materially lower regulatory risk than the reverse.

decisions.situation: Player under-paid due to the fault
decisions.treatment: Pay the difference and notify the player proactively

decisions.situation: Player over-paid due to the fault
decisions.treatment: Normally do not claw back. Assess regulatory and reputational risk before attempting recovery.
Reconstruct reasonably from the interruption point; where reconstruction is impossible, resolve in the player's favour

Refund stakes. Treatment of winnings varies by market and must be checked per profile: Connecticut bars collection of winnings, Delaware provides for forfeiture, Ontario requires cancellation and refund within 24 hours.
Refund stakes, forfeit winnings, close the account

regulatorNotification.obligationSource: Usually the licence conditions rather than public regulation. B2B suppliers normally notify the operator, who notifies the regulator - but confirm the contractual time limit, since the operator's deadline flows back to the supplier.

remediation.changeClassification: A-maths | B-rng | C-rules | D-product-constraint | E-rg | F-systems | G-disclosure | H-presentation | I-defect-fix | J-security
